artifacts.summary: 4-phase plan adopting route (b): repair the lean hard agent's handoff contract, correct the stale architecture-doc claim, add section-scoped lint Check J with a new test file, redeploy and run the full gate.

memory_candidates.content: When adding a section-scoped lint check over a family of agent-contract markdown files, measure the check's baseline against every member BEFORE designing its predicate. A predicate borrowed from an existing whole-file check can be structurally wrong for a bounded scan: in the agent-system tree, has_artifacts_object_shape greps the quoted JSON key "artifacts", but 44 of 45 handoff-writer agents state the same requirement in prose (`artifacts[] entries MUST use that schema's {type, path, summary} object shape`) rather than in a literal JSON example. Reusing the predicate unmodified would have failed 44 correct files. The general pattern: a contract requirement stated across many agent files usually has 2-3 live phrasings and 2 heading forms, so detect the semantic shape triple plus either syntactic form, never an exact-sentence match, and validate the check's PASS/FAIL partition against the whole population before writing it. A check whose baseline fails precisely the known-broken file and nothing else is the signal that the predicate is right.
